land.text: 'A smaller part of the former March of the Slavs' that 'preserved independence' when Samo's tribal union disintegrated after his death in 658

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Samo's Empire shape of 660 contains the whole Carantania shape of 661 (177 of 177 cells; my gazetteer check). The Samo's Empire page dates Samo's death '658 or 659' and says the union's fate afterwards 'is largely unclear'.

land.text: Carantania, which 'finally became a margraviate of the Carolingian Empire' in 828, its internal autonomy abolished after the anti-Frankish rebellion of Ljudevit Posavski

successors.note: Cliopatria ends Carantania in 749, not 828. The Duchy of Carinthia (Arnulf, 887) is outside this dossier.

capitals.name: Karnburg (Krnski grad)
capitals.note: 'Carantania's capital was most likely' Karnburg, 'in the Zollfeld Field, north of modern Klagenfurt'; the page gives no date, so the whole life is assumed. Coordinates approximate (about 10 km north of Klagenfurt).

keyframe_review.note: 45,562 km2 (my gazetteer check: 177 cells, Styria 65, Carinthia 36, Lower Austria 36, Slovenia 29, Salzburg 3, Upper Austria 3, Burgenland 1). The page: 'centered in the area of modern Carinthia' with parts of Styria, 'parts of southern Upper Austria and Lower Austria', 'the Lungau and Ennspongau regions of Salzburg' and 'most probably also' the Slovenian Carinthia. The shape takes all Styria and Slovenia down to 45.9 N, more than 'most probably' Slovenian Carinthia, but the page gives no southern or eastern limit. The infobox has no area, so the figure cannot be checked; kept ok, soft.

45,424 km2; no cell differs from the 661 shape. The split at 741 matches the page's turn: 'When about 740 Prince Boruth asked the Bavarian duke Odilo for help' against the Avars, 'Carantania lost its independence'; the infobox has 'Tributary to the Franks: 745'. The principality stays; it becomes a vassal (this dossier's ledger carries the Bavarian vassal tint from 743 to 788 and the Frankish one from 788 to 828, mirrored in the bavarians dossier).

correction.text: the same principality outline, unchanged: Cliopatria ends Carantania in 749 and lets its Bavarians row (750-787) absorb the shape, but the page has it a tributary under 'the overlordship of Bavaria' and the Frankish kingdom until its autonomy was abolished in 828

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a period Cliopatria lacks. 'Boruth's successors had to accept the overlordship of Bavaria'; 'By 828, internal autonomy of the principality was abolished'; 'In 828, Carantania finally became a margraviate of the Carolingian Empire'. The page also says the Avars 'had regained eastern parts of Carantania between 745 and 795' without saying which, so the outline is kept whole (soft). Same conclusion as the bavarians dossier (eu-06-f), which gives 750-787 as shape minus Carantania. The vassal tint over this keyframe is in the ledger: Bavarian 743-788, Frankish 788-828.

region.text: modern Carinthia and parts of Styria, Lower and Upper Austria and Salzburg: 'A smaller part of the former March of the Slavs preserved independence and came to be known as Carantania'

ledger.note: c. 661: Carantania emerges from the ruins of Samo's tribal union. 'In 658 Samo died and his Tribal Union disintegrated'; 'The name Carantania itself begins to appear in historical sources soon after 660'; the page says only that it 'emerged in the second half of the 7th century'. 661 is Cliopatria's year; the infobox gives 658 for Samo's death.

region.text: the Slavic principality of Carantania (modern Carinthia, parts of Styria, Lower and Upper Austria and Salzburg), as the whole principality became a Bavarian vassal

ledger.note: c. 743: Carantania becomes a vassal of Duke Odilo of Bavaria after its princes ask for help against the Avars. Duchy of Bavaria: 'At around 743, the Bavarian duke Odilo vassalised the Slavic princes of Carantania' who had asked him for protection against the invading Avars; Carantania page: 'When about 740 Prince Boruth asked the Bavarian duke Odilo for help', 'Carantania lost its independence'. The year is the Bavaria page's ('around 743'), the Carantania page says about 740; the region is my reading (the whole principality). Mirrors bavarians /ledger/6.

region.text: the whole principality, whose Bavarian overlord is deposed

ledger.note: 788: the Bavarian overlordship of Carantania ends with the fall of Duke Tassilo III. Duchy of Bavaria: 'The conquest of the Lombard Kingdom by Charlemagne entailed the fall of Tassilo, who was deposed in 788'; 'From that point, Bavaria was administered by Frankish prefects'. Neither page says what became of the Bavarian suzerainty over Carantania, so the year is a bridging judgement (confidence 1); mirrors bavarians /ledger/7.

region.text: the whole principality, tributary to the Frankish kingdom

ledger.note: 788: the Frankish kingdom becomes Carantania's sole overlord when Bavaria is taken over. Carantania page: 'Boruth's successors had to accept the overlordship of Bavaria and the semifeudal Frankish kingdom'; infobox 'Tributary to Franks: 745'. The page's 745 overlaps the Bavarian vassalage of 743-788 (Bavaria itself stood under Frankish suzerainty), so the single vassal tint passes from Bavaria to the Franks in 788, the year Bavaria came under direct Frankish rule; that year is a bridging judgement (confidence 1), not the page's.

region.text: the whole principality, now a margraviate of the Carolingian Empire

ledger.note: 828: Carantania's tributary status ends as it is absorbed into the Carolingian Empire. 'In 828, Carantania finally became a margraviate of the Carolingian Empire'; 'By 828, internal autonomy of the principality was abolished'; infobox 'Integration to Franks: 828'. The dissolve follows in the same year.

region.text: the whole principality, the margraviate of Carantania within the Carolingian Empire

ledger.note: 828: Carantania loses its autonomy and becomes a Carolingian margraviate. 'In 828, Carantania finally became a margraviate of the Carolingian Empire'; infobox 'Integrated into the Franks: 828'; the local princes were deposed for following Ljudevit Posavski's anti-Frankish rebellion, which the Ljudevit Posavski page dates to 819 ('Ljudevit raised a rebellion against his Frankish rulers in 819'); neither page dates the deposition itself, and a footnote on the Ljudevit page has the land 'administered by Bavarian counts' from 828.

wars.name: Carantanian-Avar conflict
wars.outcome: About 740 Boruth asks Duke Odilo of Bavaria for help against the Avars and Carantania loses its independence; the Avars 'had regained eastern parts of Carantania between 745 and 795'.
wars.note: Zones left empty: the page does not say which eastern parts, so no contest is drawn. The page also says that since the middle of the 8th century Carantania 'was allied with Bavaria against the Avars'. Repair round: the Pannonian Avars page does not mention Carantania; it gives the Enns as the Avar-Bavarian border in 788 ('the Avars suffered defeat' at Ybbs Field in 788) and no limits for 745-795, so the zones stay empty.

certainty.note: The page names regions (Carinthia, Styria, Lungau, Ennspongau) and no border line; the Avar frontier moved between 745 and 795 without a located line.
